chief_complaint: excruciating sudden left lower abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting with tender adnexal mass due to ovarian torsion
hpi_details: 22F college student awakened abruptly by sudden, agonizing, sharp 10/10 left lower quadrant pelvic pain radiating to her left flank and thigh. Accompanied by three episodes of vomiting and profound nausea. Pain is continuous without relief from changing positions. Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; pregnancy test negative.
ideas: in severe agony crying out from intermittent twisting pain
concerns: worried her ovary is dying or she has a ruptured ovarian cyst
expectations: wants immediate IV pain medicine, anti-nausea medication, and emergency pelvic ultrasound to check her ovary
pmh: Known 5 cm left ovarian dermoid cyst followed expectantly by gynecologist

investigation_events.title: Emergency transvaginal Doppler ultrasound
investigation_events.availability_message: The emergency Doppler ultrasound result is now available. Operative detorsion should not be delayed when clinical suspicion is high.

results.value: Enlarged edematous 6.5 x 5.0 cm left ovary containing a 4.8 cm dermoid cyst, peripheral follicles, free fluid, and absent venous and arterial flow

clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute ovarian torsion secondary to dermoid cyst evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute ovarian torsion secondary to dermoid cyst is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes STAT gynecological surgical emergency: immediately transfer patient to operating room for emergency Diagnostic Laparoscopy, surgical detorsion (untwisting the ovarian pedicle to restore perfusion), and ovarian cystectomy (enucleation of dermoid cyst while preserving healthy ovarian cortical tissue), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: excruciating sudden left lower abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting with tender adnexal mass due to ovarian torsion

Key HPI features: 22F college student awakened abruptly by sudden, agonizing, sharp 10/10 left lower quadrant pelvic pain radiating to her left flank and thigh. Accompanied by three episodes of vomiting and profound nausea. Pain is continuous without relief from changing positions. Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; pregnancy test negative.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 112, BP 134/84, Temp 37.0C. Abdomen shows marked tenderness, guarding, and localized rebound over left lower quadrant. Pelvic exam reveals a highly sensitive, enlarged, tender left adnexal mass with cervical motion tenderness. Urine pregnancy test negative. Color Doppler Transvaginal Ultrasound demonstrates an enlarged, edematous left ovary measuring 6.5 x 5.0 cm containing a 4.8 cm echogenic dermoid cyst with multiple peripheral follicles (string of pearls sign due to stromal edema), accompanied by free pelvic fluid. Doppler interrogation reveals complete absence of venous and arterial blood flow within the left ovary compared to normal flow on right.
Relevant background/PMH: Known 5 cm left ovarian dermoid cyst followed expectantly by gynecologist
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute ovarian torsion secondary to dermoid cyst.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Ruptured ovarian cyst without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Sudden onset severe unilateral pain.
management_principles: STAT gynecological surgical emergency: immediately transfer patient to operating room for emergency Diagnostic Laparoscopy, surgical detorsion (untwisting the ovarian pedicle to restore perfusion), and ovarian cystectomy (enucleation of dermoid cyst while preserving healthy ovarian cortical tissue)
Even if the ovary appears dusky or blue at initial laparoscopy, detorsion is mandatory to allow reperfusion before making any decision on oophorectomy (most ovaries recover viability in young women)
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 22F with known adnexal cyst presenting with sudden-onset unilateral pelvic pain and emesis highly concerning for acute adnexal/ovarian torsion.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 112, BP 134/84, Temp 37.0C. Abdomen shows marked tenderness, guarding, and localized rebound over left lower quadrant. Pelvic exam reveals a highly sensitive, enlarged, tender left adnexal mass with cervical motion tenderness. Urine pregnancy test negative. reference_soap.assessment: Acute Left Ovarian Torsion secondary to underlying Benign Cystic Teratoma (Dermoid Cyst).

Even if the ovary appears dusky or blue at initial laparoscopy, detorsion is mandatory to allow reperfusion before making any decision on oophorectomy (most ovaries recover viability in young women).

learning_objectives: Recognize the clinical presentation of acute ovarian torsion (abrupt unilateral pelvic pain, severe nausea/vomiting, adnexal mass)

Understand that ovarian cysts or neoplasms measuring between 5 and 10 cm (especially dermoid cysts and cystadenomas) create the highest fulcrum risk for adnexal twisting around the infundibulopelvic ligament

Interpret transvaginal Doppler ultrasound findings (ovarian enlargement >4 cm, peripheral follicle edema, absent venous/arterial Doppler flow) while knowing normal Doppler flow does NOT exclude torsion if clinical suspicion is high
Explain why laparoscopic detorsion and cystectomy with ovarian preservation is the standard of care in premenopausal women even when the ovary appears ischemic/dusky intraoperatively

teaching.diagnosis: Acute ovarian torsion secondary to dermoid cyst
teaching.one_liner: 22F with sudden severe unilateral pelvic pain, vomiting, and a known 5cm ovarian dermoid cyst.
red_flags: Continuous pain not relieved by position change

must_ask.objective: Characterize onset and continuity of pain
must_ask.say: Did the pain come on suddenly, and has it been constant since then?
Have you been told before that you have an ovarian cyst?
Is there any chance you could be pregnant?

must_ask.objective: Ask about associated nausea and vomiting
must_ask.say: Have you been vomiting along with the pain?
This pain pattern needs an urgent ultrasound and possibly surgery to save the ovary.

history.answer: Doctor, I woke up with unbearable, agonizing pain in the lower left side of my belly and I can't stop vomiting. Please help me, the pain is excruciating.
It hit me suddenly out of nowhere around 3 a.m. while I was asleep and woke me right up. It has stayed severe the entire time.
It started in the lower left part of my belly, and it has stayed focused right there without shifting anywhere else.
Yes, the pain shoots into my left flank and down into the inner side of my left thigh.
It feels like a sharp, agonizing twisting and stabbing sensation that never lets up.
It has been a continuous ten out of ten since the moment it woke me up.
Nothing relieves it at all; moving, curling up, or switching positions makes no difference, and any jarring motion makes it worse.
I've had brief mild twinges on that side once or twice over the past month, but nothing even remotely close to this agony.
I have felt intensely sick to my stomach and threw up three times, mostly clear fluid and yellowish bile with no blood.
I passed gas normally yesterday and had a normal soft bowel movement before this happened, with no diarrhea, constipation, or blood.
No, I haven't had any fever or chills.
No, my skin and eyes look normal, and my stool and urine colors haven't changed.
No burning, no urge to go frequently, and no blood in my urine.
I feel sweaty and weak from throwing up and the intense pain, but I haven't fainted or felt completely lightheaded.
No, I haven't noticed any vaginal bleeding, spotting, or unusual discharge.
No chest pain or shortness of breath; I'm just breathing fast because it hurts so much.
I just ate a standard chicken bowl for dinner last night and didn't have any alcohol.
I tried swallowing an ibuprofen after waking up, but I vomited it right back up within minutes and it did nothing.
No, I've never had any heart arrhythmias, flutterings, blood clots, or vascular diseases.
Yes, about three months ago my gynecologist told me that I have a five-centimeter dermoid cyst on my left ovary that we've been watching.
My last normal period started exactly two weeks ago, and my cycle is very regular every twenty-eight days.
I took a home urine pregnancy test right before coming in and it was negative, and I am not pregnant.
I'm terrified that the ovarian cyst might have twisted around itself and cut off the blood flow to my ovary, or that it burst.
I really need strong IV pain medicine, something to stop the vomiting, and an ultrasound right away to check my ovary.
Other than the dermoid cyst on my left ovary, I have no chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and I've never been admitted to a hospital before.
I don't take any daily prescription medications, birth control pills, or over-the-counter supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medicines, foods, or materials.
No, I don't smoke cigarettes, vape, or use any recreational drugs.
I only have an occasional glass of wine socially once or twice a month, and none this week.
I'm a senior college student living in an apartment off-campus with two roommates.
There is no family history of ovarian tumors, gynecologic cancers, or blood clotting issues.
I am not currently sexually active, and I don't use any hormonal birth control.

exam.finding: The patient appears pale, sweating, and in acute distress, writhing on the gurney from severe pelvic pain.
Blood pressure 134/84 mmHg, pulse 112 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, temperature 37.0 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99 percent on room air.
Conjunctivae are mildly pale without pallor; sclerae are clear and non-icteric.
Abdomen is flat and non-distended without surgical scars, rashes, or visible peristalsis.
Bowel sounds are hypoactive in all four quadrants; no vascular bruits are auscultated.
Marked focal tenderness and muscle guarding in the left lower quadrant; right side and upper abdomen are soft and non-tender.
Definite localized rebound tenderness over the left lower quadrant, but absent on the right.
Murphy sign is negative with no right upper quadrant tenderness or respiratory arrest on inspiration.
McBurney point tenderness, Rovsing sign, psoas sign, and obturator sign are all negative.
No punch tenderness over either bilateral costovertebral angle.
Pelvic examination reveals marked cervical motion tenderness and an exquisitely tender, enlarged mass in the left adnexal region.
